Three-Tier Architecture

Audience Framework

A scalable, operationally clear structure that supports paid media, CRM, UX/UI, content, SEO, and enrollment teams — without managing dozens of separate personas.

Strategic Positioning: Omar's behavioral archetypes are used as campaign and personalization intelligence layers beneath UAGC's scalable persona framework. This allows UAGC to preserve operational clarity while still using behavioral data to improve messaging, creative, UX, CRM, and paid media performance.

RTB Evidence

Reasons to Believe — Supporting Evidence

10 RTBs mapped to supporting data from UAGC institutional reporting, GA4 audience data, EAB/Lumina-Gallup research, Omar's structural comparison, and Dentsu's survey. Dentsu n=100 — treat as directional only, not statistically significant.

Dentsu signal Confirms Contradicts Weak / Mixed Signal Not surveyed
No Standardized Testing Required
The highest-anxiety re-entry barrier — removed before the conversation starts
Not surveyed by Dentsu
Returning Student Transfer Student Career Changer All Audiences
Supporting Evidence
UAGC Data 2023–24
69.6% of bachelor's graduates are working adults 30–49 — people who haven't taken a standardized test in 10–25 years. Requiring one signals "we're not built for you."
UAGC Data 2023–24
49.1% of bachelor's graduates are Pell-eligible — a population for whom test prep is an additional unaffordable cost and time barrier.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
Only 25% of adults without a degree believe quality, affordable education is accessible to most people. Test requirements reinforce this belief — removing them directly contradicts it.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
Stopped-out adults are nearly 2× more likely to consider re-enrolling. They left due to life circumstances, not academic failure — standardized tests re-trigger that failure anxiety.
Generous Transfer Policy
Prior credits count — military training, community college, professional certifications
Dentsu: Contradicts — label confusion, not value rejection
Transfer Student AZ Transfer Active Duty Veteran Returning Student
Supporting Evidence
EAB 2025
Program length/time-to-completion is the #2 enrollment criterion after cost. Transfer credits eliminate both barriers simultaneously — shorter time and lower total cost.
UAGC Data 2023–24
Military-affiliated students represent 31.9% of all bachelor's completions. JST, CCAF, and ACE credit recognition is the non-negotiable first question for nearly 1 in 3 UAGC graduates.
Omar Structural Comparison 1.4
Credit transparency is the #1 structural conversion lever in UAGC's paid page data. Pages that answer the credit question early hold transfer-intent visitors significantly longer.
GA4 Apr 2025–Apr 2026
18–24 band engages for 84 seconds but converts at only 2.2% — the lowest of any age group. Credit uncertainty is the most credible explanation for high engagement with low conversion.
NSC Fall 2024
19.7% growth in nontraditional enrollment (age 21+). This entire growth segment has prior credits somewhere — community college, military training, or professional certification.
Dentsu Survey
"Transfer-friendly" ranked in the least important chart but the slide notes it "may need further explanation." The label is the problem, not the value — behavioral data at scale directly contradicts this finding.
$0 Application Fee
Complete cost transparency at the very first action — the first step costs nothing
Not surveyed by Dentsu
All Audiences Returning Student Career Changer Employer Sponsored
Supporting Evidence
EAB 2025
60% of adult learners removed a school from consideration because the program seemed too expensive — often before ever contacting an advisor. $0 application fee is the inverse signal: complete transparency from the first action.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
57% of unenrolled adults have considered enrolling in the past 2 years but haven't acted. $0 fee removes the "what if I'm not ready" financial risk from the first step.
GA4 Apr 2025–Apr 2026
The 45–54 band generates 12,455 key events with no dedicated campaign — a considering-but-not-acting audience. $0 fee directly addresses hesitation without financial commitment.
Omar Structural Comparison 1.4
3.23× rage-click recurrence on the RFI form with 0.04% conversion per click. $0 application fee signals low-risk entry and belongs above the fold alongside the form.
WSCUC Accredited
Regional accreditation through WASC — employer-recognized, nationally respected
Dentsu: Confirms — top value prop in both survey and behavioral data
Career Advancement Employer Sponsored Military Transfer Student All Audiences
Supporting Evidence
Dentsu Survey — Most Important
Accredited ranked among the most important value props at ~40 mentions. Direct quote: "We need credentials that will be recognized in the workplace and not just looking good on the wall." — Military respondent.
Omar Structural Comparison 1.4
TRUST-02 (accreditation module) present on pages converting at 7–13%, absent on all three pages bouncing at 68–72%. Direct behavioral evidence that accreditation visibility reduces bounce.
EAB 2025
54% of adult learners enroll for career advancement or career change. Accreditation is the institutional proof the credential will be recognized — it's the ROI guarantee.
SVA Census 2024
62% of student veterans are first-generation college students. Accreditation signals legitimacy to an audience with limited institutional trust baseline.
UAGC Corporate Partnerships
1,500+ employer partners including Mayo Clinic, Banner Health, State Farm, and T-Mobile. Regional accreditation is what makes these partnerships credible and transferable.
100% Online
No campus, no commute — fully online and built for adults with full lives
Dentsu: Confirms — highest-rated value prop in Dentsu survey
Military Spouse Active Duty Career Advancement Returning Student All Audiences
Supporting Evidence
Dentsu Survey — Most Important
100% online ranked as the #1 most important value prop at ~62 mentions — highest score in the entire survey. Direct quote: "As a mother of young kids, I need flexibility." — Military respondent.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
Scheduling conflicts with work are the #2 cited barrier to enrollment. Fully online directly removes this barrier — not as a feature, but as a life enabler.
UAGC Data 2023–24
60.4% of bachelor's graduates are female. For military spouses, caregivers, and working parents, fully online is not a preference — it is a requirement.
GA4 Apr 2025–Apr 2026
Mobile engagement dominates UAGC traffic. The "online" experience must be mobile-first — the channel and the product are the same thing for this audience.
Study at Your Own Pace
Async, 5-week courses — built around your schedule, not a campus calendar
Dentsu: Confirms — second highest-rated value prop in Dentsu survey
Military Spouse Returning Student Career Advancement Active Duty
Supporting Evidence
Dentsu Survey — Most Important
"Study at your own pace" ranked second at ~45 mentions. Direct quote: "As a mother of young kids, I need flexibility." — Military respondent.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
Scheduling conflicts with work are the #2 enrollment barrier. Async, self-paced courses are the structural solution — not just a marketing claim.
EAB 2025
Program length is the #2 enrollment criterion. Flexible pacing allows students to accelerate or slow down based on life demands — directly addressing this concern.
UAGC Data 2023–24
80% of UAGC students work full-time while studying (per UA Faculty Senate report). Self-paced format is not a convenience feature — it's the product design for this entire audience.
Multiple / Flexible Start Dates
Start when you're ready — not when a semester opens
Dentsu: Confirms directionally
All Audiences
Supporting Evidence
Dentsu Survey — Most Important
Flexible start dates ranked ~30 mentions — a meaningful directional signal that "when can I start?" is an active decision factor for this audience.
EAB 2025
Cost and time-to-completion are the top two enrollment criteria. Flexible start dates reduce time-to-enrollment — faster decision, faster start, faster completion.
Omar Structural Comparison 1.4
Dynamic upcoming start dates confirmed as a UX requirement across all landing pages. Surfacing a concrete next start date creates a decision point and is a proven conversion lever.
Lumina-Gallup 2025
57% of unenrolled adults considered enrolling in the past 2 years. A visible upcoming start date converts consideration into action by making the choice time-bound without pressure.
Career Services — For Life
Employer connections, resume support, and career advising — available after you graduate
Dentsu: Weak signal — likely awareness gap, not indifference
Career Advancement Veteran Employer Sponsored Transfer Student
Supporting Evidence
UAGC Press Release, Feb 2026
Access to nearly 98,000 employers and 64,000+ active job postings through Handshake. In Fall 2025, 4,845 students activated accounts and 2,047 took action. Available to students and alumni for life.
UAGC Corporate Partnerships
1,500+ employer partners including Mayo Clinic, Blue Cross Blue Shield, T-Mobile, State Farm, Banner Health, and Wounded Warrior Project.
EAB 2025
54% enroll for career advancement or career change. Career services extends the value prop beyond the degree — it's the post-enrollment proof that the investment pays off.
Dentsu Survey — Least Important
Career services access ranked ~25 on the least important chart. This likely reflects an awareness gap — students may not know what the service includes — rather than indifference to career outcomes.
Returning Student Career Changer All Audiences
Supporting Evidence
Credits for Work / Life Experience
Your professional experience may count toward your degree
Dentsu: Mixed signal — awareness gap likely driving the split
Career Advancement Returning Student Veteran Employer Sponsored
Supporting Evidence
EAB 2025
Program length is the #2 enrollment criterion. Work and life experience credits reduce time-to-completion — the same two-barrier eliminator as transfer credits, applied to a different source of prior learning.
UAGC Data 2023–24
69.6% of bachelor's graduates are working adults 30–49. This audience has 10–25 years of professional experience that may have academic equivalency — a differentiator most competitors don't surface prominently.
SVA Census 2024
25% of student veterans enroll to change careers, 20% to be more competitive in the job market. Military training and service experience as credits directly bridges their service record to civilian credentials.
Dentsu Survey — Mixed
Credits for work experience appeared in both most (~20) and least (~12) important charts. Split signal suggests audience awareness varies — some value it highly once they know it exists; others haven't considered it applies to them.

Paid Media Destinations

Priority Landing Pages

8 conversion-focused landing pages — one per Tier 2 persona. Each page shows UX priorities, CRO requirements, and links to the layout scoring tool where designers can build and score the module structure before development.

Paid Landing Page

Career Advancement

Persona: Wendy Bosquez · Career Advancement Student
Explore layout alternatives in Omar's Layout Builder →
Base Components Required on all paid landing pages
  • Mobile-first hero with clear CTA
  • Short inquiry form / reduced-friction RFI
  • Upcoming start dates
  • Tuition / benefit transparency
  • Student or alumni quote
  • Career outcome section (job titles, salary ranges)
  • Trust signals
  • FAQ section
  • Dynamic Tier 3 emotional motivation module
Audience-Specific Components Unique to this persona
  • Salary growth visualization by program
  • Employer-recognized credential callout
  • Program options aligned to career advancement goals
  • Credit for experience / prior learning section
  • Program comparison by career outcome
Page Priority Sequence Audience-decision-first · top to bottom wireframe order
#ComponentAudience QuestionValue Prop ThemesUX / UI Intent
1 Hero Is this designed for someone like me? Career-Focused Education · Built for Adults · Flexible Online Learning Identity recognition — establish relevance for working adults balancing career and life
2 Start Dates How soon can I begin? Multiple Start Dates · Flexible Timing · Begin When Ready Create momentum without pressure — dynamic dates reduce hesitation
3 Tuition Transparency Can I realistically afford this? Tuition Clarity · Financial Aid · Credit Recognition Reduce financial uncertainty — address the #1 reason adult learners disengage
4 Inquiry Form How do I take the first step? Simple Next Step · No Overload · Clear Path Forward Accessible entry point — short form, low friction, above or sticky
5 Career Outcome Section Will this help me move forward? Career Growth · Workforce Skills · Professional Goals Connect education to future opportunity — job titles, salary context by program

Tactical Execution

Four-Phase Launch Roadmap

A phased rollout from audience alignment through optimization — building the paid landing page ecosystem in layers.

1

Audience Alignment & Strategy

Days 0–30 · Foundation

Deliverables
  • Finalize Tier 1–3 framework and confirm persona ownership
  • Align Paid, CRM, UX/UI, Content, SEO, DX, and Admissions
  • Define landing page requirements and confirm student/alumni story usage
  • Build creative testing matrix
Paid MediaCRMUX/UISEODXAdmissionsContent
2

Paid Landing Page Development

Days 30–90 · Build

Priority Pages
  • Career Advancement · Finish Your Degree · Transfer Credits
  • Employer Tuition Benefits · Military Advancement
  • Veteran Career Transition · Military Spouse Flexibility
  • Arizona Transfer Pathway
UX/UI Requirements
Mobile-first layoutClear hero CTA Reduced-friction formStudent quote module Career outcome sectionTuition/benefit clarity Trust signalsFAQ section Dynamic upcoming start dates
Content Requirements
  • Student or alumni story matched to the target persona — peer proof is one of the highest-converting trust signals for adult learners
  • Career outcomes with specific job titles and salary ranges sourced from BLS or O*NET — adult learners require career validation before inquiry
  • Tuition or benefit cost stated clearly — cost opacity is the #1 reason adult learners remove a school from consideration
3

Campaign Activation

Days 90–120 · Launch

Channel Priorities
  • Google Search — primary intent capture
  • Performance Max — broad reach optimization
  • YouTube — trust and awareness building
  • Meta — persona targeting (Facebook + Instagram)
  • Retargeting — /success page visitors, 30-day window
  • LinkedIn — employer-sponsored and career advancement only
Campaign Structure
Tier 2 = campaign / persona structureTier 3 = ad copy + keyword themes + variants
4

Optimization & Personalization

Days 120–180 · Scale

Deliverables
  • A/B test hero copy and student quote placement by persona
  • Test short vs. long form inquiry paths
  • Add dynamic program modules and personalize by audience source
  • Build CRM branching logic by persona and Tier 3 archetype
  • Add retargeting audiences based on page behavior
  • Optimize based on CTR, conversion rate, engagement time, and form completion
Performance Framework

KPI Framework

Primary KPIs tracked across paid campaigns, landing pages, and CRM journeys — measured at the Tier 2 persona level.

CTR
Improve relevance through persona-matched ad copy and Tier 3 archetype variations
Landing Page Conversion Rate
Increase inquiries via friction reduction, trust signals, and barrier-specific messaging
Cost Per Inquiry
Reduce CPL through tighter persona targeting and higher landing page relevance
Form Completion Rate
Increase via simplified, persona-specific forms with progressive disclosure
Engagement Time
Build trust through career outcome content, testimonials, and benefit clarity modules
Bounce Rate
Reduce via personalized first experiences matched to audience source and ad message
Returning Visitor Conversion
Improve re-engagement via retargeting sequences and barrier-specific objection pages
CRM Click-Through Rate
Improve nurture performance through Tier 3 archetype-based branching and personalization
Persona-Level Campaign Performance
Track CTR, conversion, and CPL at the Tier 2 persona level to inform budget allocation
